subject: Solara Health MAP: anchoring proposal + staggered acceptance safeguard
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@solarahealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hwang <tom.hwang@solarahealth.com>, Solara Procurement <procurement@solarahealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & acceptance windows — request to re-anchor

Hi Lauren,

Quick note from our side after this morning's internal readout: the clinical integration sprint will slip by ~10 business days due to a vendor cert timing issue. That pushes our planned evaluation week and affects the go-live target.

We need to understand what that means for the MAP dates and any commercial accommodations — specifically credits or an expanded acceptance window. Can you share an updated MAP that reflects staggered acceptance and an approach for minimizing risk to the go-live?

Thanks,
Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Platform Integrations
Solara Health

Attachments: none

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@solarahealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-07T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & acceptance windows — request to re-anchor

Jane — thanks for the heads up and the context. I spoke with engineering and PMs to draft a two-track approach that protects your timeline while keeping the eval quality high. Summary below; I'll attach a redline MAP after this note.

1) Anchor date vs. soft-go: propose we keep the public "anchor" go-live date but move the formal acceptance window to a staggered model (phase A + phase B) so you can ship non-clinical flows first. This preserves marketing and scheduling commitments while buying the integration work time.

2) Evaluation plan: split the evaluation into a short smoke acceptance (3 business days) for core infra and a longer clinical acceptance (10 business days) for workflows that depend on vendor certs. We will provide test harnesses and sample prompts for the clinical flows.

3) Commercial: open to a partial credit or milestone-based credit tied to the delayed clinical acceptance. Ben — can you outline typical credit bands here so we have something concrete?

4) Risk log & mitigations: Camila will maintain a running risk register for the integration items; Grace will own exec escalation if we hit the hard date.

I'll attach: Solara_MAP_v3.xlsx (redline), eval-checklist-weekly.csv, and a suggested draft email for procurement. Please confirm if the staggered model is acceptable and we will circulate final MAP and shared Drive link.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Solara_MAP_v3.xlsx (redline), eval-checklist-weekly.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@solarahealth.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-07T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & acceptance windows — credit bands and options

Lauren / Jane — quick commercial options from my side:

- Option 1: 10% one-time credit applied if clinical acceptance extends beyond the original MAP by >7 business days.
- Option 2: Milestone credit: 5% credit once smoke acceptance passes, and additional 5% on clinical acceptance completion (total 10%).
- Option 3: Time-bound extension with no credit for startups: extend acceptance windows by 14 days if procurement approves.

I'm attaching the credit-request-form.pdf for procurement if you want to route for approval. If Solara prefers a revenue-neutral path, Option 2 preserves economics while giving risk protection.

Ben
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachment: credit-request-form.pdf

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@solarahealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-08T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & acceptance windows — technical risk register populated

Following up with a short technical ledger. I've populated the risk register inside Solara_MAP_v3.xlsx (tab: risk_log). Highlights:

- Vendor cert delay (priority HIGH): current ETA +10 business days. Impact: clinical flows blocked until cert in staging. Mitigation: we can provision a stubbed service in staging to run the majority of acceptance tests; that will validate infra and API integration.
- KV cache alignment (priority MED): small tokenization mismatch affecting a subset of prompts; workaround available in client config.
- Load profile tests (priority LOW): scheduled this week; results will inform final autoscaling configs.

Ask to Solara: can your integration lead provide the vendor's cert ETA and a short call with the vendor contact this week? If we get a target, we can commit precise acceptance dates for phase B.

Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Doe <jane.doe@solarahealth.com>, Tom Hwang <tom.hwang@solarahealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-11T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP & acceptance windows — exec escalation (if needed)

Looping in a short escalation path: if the vendor cert slips beyond Oct 25th, I'll escalate to our VP of Sales and request a senior commercial review to approve accelerated credits or prioritized engineering support.

Also recommend a joint daily stand (15m) for the next 10 business days between our SRE/Integration leads to keep the MAP risk register live. Camila — can you host? Ben — want to be on the stand for any procurement gating?

Grace
Head of Accounts Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@solarahealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-13T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP & acceptance windows — confirmation of staggered approach and next steps

Thanks all — we reviewed the proposed staggered acceptance and the two-option commercial approach. Procurement prefers Option 2 (milestone credit) and procurement will sign the redline MAP once we get the vendor ETA confirmed.

Action items we confirmed:
- Solara: vendor will confirm cert ETA by 2027-10-18.
- Camila: provision stubbed service in staging by 2027-10-15 so Redwood can run smoke acceptance.
- Ben & Lauren: prepare a short procurement packet with Option 2 language and the credit-request-form; we'll route to legal.
- Weekly stand: daily 15m standups starting 2027-10-14 (Camila to host).

We appreciate the flexible approach — this keeps our go-live commitments intact while giving space to resolve the integration item. Please circulate the final MAP redline and a one-page note for our procurement team.

Jane
Jane Doe
Head of Platform Integrations
Solara Health
